territorial_scope.description: Applies as a California statute to systems and advertising within the state's Business and Professions Code framework; the text contains no explicit extraterritorial reach.

evidence.quote: The people of the State of California do enact as follows:

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Adds Business and Professions Code Chapter 15.5, which prohibits using health-profession license terms in the advertising or functionality of AI or GenAI systems where they imply care is given by a licensed person. Enforced by health care licensing boards; each use is a separate violation.
summary.long: Adds Chapter 15.5 (Health Advice From Artificial Intelligence) to Division 2 of the Business and Professions Code. Section 4999.8 defines AI and GenAI by reference to Government Code Sections 11546.45.5 and 11549.64, and defines health care profession as any profession subject to licensure or regulation under the Division or an initiative act referred to in it. Section 4999.9(c) prohibits using a term, letter or phrase in the advertising or functionality of an AI or GenAI system that indicates or implies that the care, advice, reports or assessments offered are provided by a licensed natural person. Section 4999.9(b) makes existing Division provisions that bar specified license-indicating terms enforceable against a person or entity that develops or deploys such a system. Section 4999.9(a) places violations under the jurisdiction of the appropriate licensing board or enforcement agency, which may seek an injunction or restraining order under Section 125.5, and preserves other remedies. Section 4999.9(d) treats each use of a prohibited term as a separate violation. Section 2 is a state-mandate clause stating that no reimbursement is required for local agencies or school districts. The text states no effective date and sets no fines or penalty amounts.

notes: The text states no effective date, no penalty amount and no private right of action. Violations fall under existing licensing and enforcement authority in the Business and Professions Code (§ 4999.9(a)). SEC. 2 describes the act as creating or changing a crime or infraction, but no provision of this text creates a crime or sets a penalty. The AI and GenAI definitions are incorporated by reference from the Government Code and are not reproduced here. obligations.summary: Prohibits using a term, letter or phrase in the advertising or functionality of an AI or GenAI system where it indicates or implies that the care, advice, reports or assessments are given by a licensed natural person. Under (b), provisions of the Division barring such terms without a license are enforceable against a person or entity that develops or deploys such a system. Each use is a separate violation under (d), which is enforcement and not coded here.
